cases.query: Testing just one nonzero functional always decides whether f(x)=y is solvable.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: For f:ℚ→ℚ², f(t)=(t,0), let y=(0,1). The first-coordinate functional does not annihilate all outputs, so its conditional test is vacuous even though the system is insoluble. All annihilating functionals are required.

cases.query: A nontrivial kernel makes every right-hand side solvable.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: The zero map ℚ→ℚ has a nontrivial kernel, but f(x)=1 has no solution. The theorem constructs another solution only from an existing one.

cases.query: AB=I makes A injective as well as B.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: Take A=(1 0):ℚ²→ℚ and B=(1,0)ᵀ:ℚ→ℚ². Then AB=I, but A(0,1)=0, so A is not injective.

cases.query: The products differ even if the coefficient t is zero or the indices coincide.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: If t=0 both products vanish; if i=j both are scalar multiples of the same diagonal unit. Both hypotheses in the positive card are essential.

cases.query: Any finite geometric sum is an inverse of I−N without the condition N^k=0.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: Over ℚ take N=2I and k=2 in a positive dimension. The sum is 3I while (I−N)3I=−3I, not I. The uncancelled remainder is −N^k.

cases.query: Membership in S+T means membership in the set union S∪T.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: For the two coordinate lines in ℚ², (1,1) belongs to their sum but neither line.

cases.query: The union of any two subspaces fails closure under addition.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: If S⊆T then S∪T=T is itself a subspace. The two incomparability assumptions distinguish precisely the constructive counterexample case.

cases.query: All linear maps preserve intersections of subspaces under direct image.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: Let f:ℚ²→ℚ be f(x,y)=x+y. For S=span(e₁) and T=span(e₂), S∩T=0 but f(S)=f(T)=ℚ. The common image need not have a common preimage without injectivity.

cases.query: It is enough to check relations whose coefficients are all equal.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: For v=(1,2) in the ℚ-space ℚ, a(1+2)=0 forces a=0, but the relation 2·1−1·2=0 is nontrivial. All coefficient functions must be tested.

cases.query: Every finite spanning family gives unique coefficients.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: The family (1,1) spans ℚ, but the vector 1 has coefficient choices (1,0) and (0,1). Existence of coefficients does not imply independence.

cases.query: A finite family with pairwise distinct nonzero vectors must be independent.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: The distinct nonzero vectors e₁,e₂,e₁+e₂ in ℚ² are dependent. Repetition is a sufficient obstruction, not the only obstruction.

cases.query: Independence is preserved by every linear map, regardless of its kernel on the span.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: The nonzero single-vector family (1) is independent in ℚ, but the zero map sends it to (0). Its span meets the kernel nontrivially, so the restriction hypothesis fails.

cases.query: A spanning family alone is the family of a basis with those exact indices.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: The family (1,1) spans ℚ but is dependent and cannot be the values of any two-element basis. Both spanning and independence are required.

cases.query: Every family of dim V vectors spans V.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: For any nonempty finite basis, the positive card constructs a same-length family by replacing one basis vector by zero. The corresponding coordinate functional separates the removed vector from the new span.

cases.query: Every affine translation is linear because it preserves differences.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: For any nonzero translation vector u, translation sends 0 to u≠0, violating the zero-preservation law of a linear map. If u=0 it is the identity, so the nonzero premise matters.

cases.query: If p∘q=0 then p=0 or q=0.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: For any basis with two distinct indices, coordinate projections onto those two basis lines are nonzero while their composite vanishes. No special matrix size or numerical coefficient is needed.

cases.query: Range and kernel of every endomorphism are complementary.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: On ℚ² let f(x,y)=(y,0). Its range and kernel are both span(e₁), so their intersection is nonzero and their sum is not the whole space. Here f²=0≠f.

cases.query: For rectangular A and B, det(AB)=det(BA) without adding identities.
cases.counterexample_or_missing_premise: Take A=(1 0):ℚ²→ℚ and B=(1,0)ᵀ:ℚ→ℚ². AB has determinant 1, while BA=diag(1,0) has determinant 0. The identity shifts in Sylvester’s formula are essential.
